# **Evidence-Validated Multi-AI Operating System: Architecture, Playbook Audit, and Staged Implementation Blueprint**

**Executive Verdict:** Building an evidence-validated AI operating system across Anthropic Claude/Claude Code, OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex, and Google Antigravity requires rejecting the assumption that all three ecosystems must collaborate on every workflow1. Official vendor documentation verified on 28 October 2026 and parametric operating-cost models indicate that **a single primary platform paired with deterministic software scripts and OS-enforced sandboxes is the Pareto-efficient baseline for routine engineering, quantitative coding, and focused research**1. In our parametric Total Cost per Verified Successful Outcome (TCVSO) scenario model (an analytical estimate awaiting live pilot confirmation on your hardware), expanding to a **two-platform architecture**—using Git worktree isolation or structured file handoffs so a second model family conducts independent adversarial verification or browser-based end-to-end testing—reduces modeled TCVSO by 20% to 45% on correctness-critical quantitative backtesting and complex multi-file software refactors by catching silent defects before human review3. Conversely, **three-platform automated orchestration and multi-agent swarms** multiply token consumption by up to 7× in plan mode, invalidate prompt caches across model switches, and introduce state-synchronisation fragility, failing minimum-complexity acceptance gates for solo operators and small teams unless strictly confined to embarrassingly parallel, read-only exploration4.  
In strict compliance with ACTION\_LAUNCH\_PROMPT.md, MASTER\_RESEARCH\_PROMPT.md (covering all 26 Parts and 78 numbered requirements), and the mandatory Research Governance and Decision Protocol (multi\_ai\_red\_team\_findings.zip), this report executes **Gate 0 (Scope and Requirements)** and **Gate 1 (Capability Verification and Playbook Audit)** in full, while delivering the consolidated **Deliverables A through H** engineering specification1. All attached packages—including the \# Claude Efficiency Playbook: Cutting Usage Without Cutting Quality (October 2026)—have been inspected in their entirety3. Where empirical validation requires live execution inside your authenticated subscriptions, local host environment, or paid API budgets, protocols are preregistered and clearly marked **Proposed (Blocked at Gate 1/2 Pending User Authorisation)**, never fabricated or conflated with desk-verified documentation1.

## **PART II — DELIVERABLE B: STAGE 1 INDIVIDUAL PLATFORM OPTIMISATION & CLAUDE PLAYBOOK AUDIT**

### **5\. Item-by-Item Technical Audit of the Attached Claude Efficiency Playbook (October 2026\)**

Per Section 12 of MASTER\_RESEARCH\_PROMPT.md, every substantive recommendation in your attached \# Claude Efficiency Playbook: Cutting Usage Without Cutting Quality (October 2026\)5 has been audited against official Anthropic documentation current as of 28 October 20266.  
The attached playbook is grounded in late-2026 Anthropic mechanics, but our audit identified **four critical technical nuances and documentation conflicts** that will silently waste quota or degrade output quality if not corrected. First, regarding the **/model opusplan Prompt-Cache Trap**, the playbook recommends /model opusplan (Action \#4) while advising in Section 2.3 to avoid switching models mid-task because model switches bust the prompt cache5. Official Claude Code prompt-caching documentation (code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching) explicitly warns that **opusplan mode toggles between Opus and Sonnet and recomputes the entire request uncached on the switch**7. Consequently, opusplan only yields net savings if the execution phase runs for multiple turns on Sonnet or generates large output volumes where Sonnet's \$10/MTok vs. Opus's \$20/MTok output rate outweighs the uncached prefix rebuild7.  
Second, regarding the **@file vs. Bare File Path Contradiction**, Playbook Action \#6 advises writing bare paths (src/strategy.py) rather than @src/strategy.py because @ injects the entire file plus its CLAUDE.md directory tree5. While Help Center article 14552983 states this16, Help Center article 14553240 ("Give Claude context: CLAUDE.md and better prompts") and code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows state the opposite: **when you already know the exact target file, using @path/to/file (up to 25,000 tokens or 256 KB) is faster and consumes fewer tokens** because it avoids multiple exploratory Grep and Read tool-call turns26. The optimal rule is size-gated: use @file for known, small-to-medium target files (\<5,000 tokens) and bare paths for large files, logs, or exploratory directories16.  
Third, regarding **Unified Chat \+ Cowork Removing the Manual Web Search Toggle**, Playbook Action \#7 advises toggling off Web Search in chat5. Per Help Center articles 10684626 and 16761823 ("Claude Cowork and chat are one Claude"), accounts migrated to the unified Chat/Cowork experience **no longer have a manual Web Search toggle**; Claude triggers web searches automatically unless instructed otherwise in the prompt ("Do not search the web")36. Fourth, regarding **Compaction Token Survival Limits (v2.1.198+ / v2.1.304+)**, the playbook notes /compact summarises history5, but omits the deterministic survival caps documented in code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window: after compaction, only the **5 most recently modified files** are re-read in full (any file exceeding 5,000 tokens is demoted to a path pointer), invoked skill bodies are capped at **5,000 tokens per skill (25,000 tokens total)**, and since v2.1.198, the compaction request itself inherits Extended Thinking if active, burning substantial output tokens47.

### **6\. Cross-Platform Economics and Prompt-Caching Verification**

To ground platform selection in deterministic calculation rather than informal rules of thumb, we verified the exact API token rates and prompt-caching break-even thresholds across Anthropic Claude 5.5/Fable, OpenAI GPT-6/6.1, and Google Gemini 4/3.8 as of 28 October 20264.  
![][image9]  
Three structural insights emerge from this cross-platform pricing verification. First, while mid-tier pricing has converged, cache TTL mechanics diverge substantially across vendors. Anthropic's **Claude Sonnet 5.5**, OpenAI's **GPT-6.1 Sol**, and Google's **Gemini 4 Argon** (under introductory pricing through 30 November 2026\) share the exact same headline rate of **\$2.00/MTok input, \$10.00/MTok output, and \$0.10/MTok cached input read (a 95% discount)**4. However, Anthropic charges \$2.50/MTok (1.25×) for a **5-minute** cache write and \$4.00/MTok (2.0×) for a **1-hour** cache write on Sonnet 5.5, and its Claude 4.7+ tokenizer produces **approximately 30% to 35% more tokens** for the same source text than earlier tokenizers4. By contrast, OpenAI charges \$2.50/MTok (1.25×) for a **30-minute** cache write—providing 6× longer cache retention than Anthropic's 5-minute tier at the same 1.25× write multiplier—and \$5.00/MTok (2.5×) for a **12-hour** cache write on GPT-6.1 Sol4. Meanwhile, Google's **Gemini 4 Argon** uses **implicit caching only** (explicit caching is unsupported on Argon), discounting cached input by 95% to $0.10/MTok($0.20/MTok starting 1 December 2026\) without an explicit write surcharge, whereas **Gemini 3.8 Flash** charges \$0.075/MTok per read plus a \$0.50/MTok-hour storage fee for explicit caches20.  
Second, mid-session model switching is financially destructive to cached workflows. For a 100,000-token repository context over 10 turns on Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol, keeping a warm cache costs **\$0.34** (\$0.25 initial write plus 9 reads at \$0.01 each), whereas busting the cache on every turn costs **\$2.00**—nearly a **6× input cost multiplier**4. Even a single mid-session cache invalidation (from toggling /model opusplan, adding an MCP server, or running /compact when /rewind would suffice) immediately adds \$0.25 in uncached write overhead on Sonnet 5.5 or \$1.25 on Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra4.  
Third, speed modes and multi-agent modes impose steep quota multipliers. Anthropic's **Opus 5.5 Fast Mode** doubles API rates to **\$8.00/MTok input and \$40.00/MTok output** and maintains an independent cache from standard speed7. OpenAI's **Fast Mode** consumes included subscription quota at **2.5×** the standard rate (2× on purchased credits), while **Ultrafast Mode** (exclusive to Pro \$500 and eligible Enterprise/Edu plans for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol) burns included subscription allowance at **8×** the standard rate (6× on purchased credits)19.

### **7\. Standalone Platform Playbooks (Verified October 2026\)**

#### **7.1 Revised Independent Playbook: Anthropic Claude & Claude Code**

**Surface and Entitlement Separation:** Across the Anthropic ecosystem, claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Mobile, Cowork, Claude Design, Xcode integration, and interactive Claude Code all draw from the **same rolling 5-hour session limit and fixed-day weekly limit**5. Monthly API credits included with Max 5x ($100/month),Max20x($200/month), and Team (\$20/Standard seat, \$100/Premium seat, pooled up to \$500/month) cover only the Claude API, Managed Agents, and self-invoked claude \-p or Agent SDK runs authenticated via a linked Claude Console API key; they **never** cover interactive Claude Code or app overages, and expire monthly without rollover30. Because Claude Code prioritises the ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY environment variable over /login subscription authentication, you must never export ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY in \~/.zshrc or \~/.bashrc on a Pro or Max machine, or interactive terminal sessions will silently bill your Console API balance22. Always run /status at session start to confirm active subscription authentication22.  
**Context and Instruction Architecture (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, .claude/skills/):** Keep your root ./CLAUDE.md under **150 lines** containing only build/test/lint commands, core architectural invariants, and "two-strike" corrections26. Offload directory- or language-specific rules into .claude/rules/\*.md using YAML frontmatter paths: globs (for example, paths: \["src/cbot/\*\*/\*.cs"\]) so rules enter the context window **only** when Claude reads or edits matching files26. Package repeatable multi-step procedures (such as /backtest-audit or /ship) into .claude/skills/\<name\>/SKILL.md with disable-model-invocation: true for manual-only workflows so even their descriptions consume zero initial context tokens, and use \!command\`\` lines inside SKILL.md to inject pre-computed deterministic shell output (such as \`git status \--short\`) before the model runs26. Periodically run \`/doctor prompt-audit\` (requires Claude Code \`v2.1.283+\`) to detect contradictory instructions across \`CLAUDE.md\`, \`AGENTS.md\`, and skills26.  
**Deterministic Control via Lifecycle Hooks (.claude/settings.json):** Because CLAUDE.md instructions are model-discretionary26, enforce mandatory guardrails deterministically via lifecycle hooks in .claude/settings.json24. Configure a PreToolUse hook on the Bash tool that intercepts pytest, dotnet test, or backtest commands and pipes output through grep \-A 5 \-E '(FAIL\|ERROR\|error:)' \| head \-100, shrinking verbose test logs from tens of thousands of tokens to a few hundred27. Add a second PreToolUse hook matching Edit\|Write that returns "permissionDecision": "deny" if the target touches data/raw/, .env\*, or migration history24. Configure a SessionStart hook with "matcher": "compact" to re-inject critical sprint invariants immediately after context compaction, and a Stop hook that runs your deterministic test suite and returns {"decision": "block"} if any test fails, preventing premature completion reports (T11)11.  
**Subagent and Worktree Concurrency:** Use built-in Explore (read-only) or custom subagents (.claude/agents/\<name\>.md with model: haiku or sonnet, omitClaudeMd: true when repo rules are unnecessary, and maxTurns caps) to isolate noisy codebase searches or log triage from the main conversation's 1-hour cache7. For parallel feature implementation, launch separate terminal sessions in isolated Git worktrees (claude \--worktree \<feature-name\>) rather than enabling experimental Agent Teams (CLAUDE\_CODE\_EXPERIMENTAL\_AGENT\_TEAMS=1), which consume approximately 7× more tokens in plan mode, cannot resume in-process teammates via /resume, and exhibit task-status lag5.

#### **7.2 Independent Playbook: OpenAI ChatGPT Work & Codex (v0.159.0+)**

**Surface, Model, and Quota Architecture:** ChatGPT Work (web and desktop) and Codex (CLI, IDE extension, desktop app, and cloud) share your plan's usage allowance and credit pool when authenticated via ChatGPT sign-in19. Plus ($20/month)andStandardBusiness($20–\$25/user/month) enforce a **5-hour local message window** (estimated at 5–45 messages for gpt-6-astra, 15–160 for gpt-6.1-sol, 35–285 for gpt-6.1-terra, and 350–3,000 for gpt-6-luna) alongside weekly limits, whereas **Pro (\$100, \$200, and \$500/month) currently has no 5-hour limit**19. Note that grandfathered higher Pro 200 allowances expire after **29 October 2026**, transitioning to the updated lower Pro 200 baseline19. For model routing, set **gpt-6.1-sol** (default 500,000-token context window, $2/$10 API rate, 50/250 credits/MTok) at medium reasoning effort as your primary workhorse for repository engineering, multi-source synthesis, and quantitative pipeline development, escalating to xhigh only when resolving conflicting evidence or complex architecture19. Route high-volume extraction, log triage, and narrow subagents (agents.default\_subagent\_model \= "gpt-6-luna") to **gpt-6-luna** ($0.10/$0.50 API rate, 2.5/12.5 credits/MTok), which is 20× cheaper than gpt-6.1-sol and 100× cheaper than gpt-6-astra8. Use **gpt-6.1-terra** ($1/$5 API rate, 25/125 credits/MTok, requiring Codex CLI v0.159.0+) for visual chart/screenshot interpretation and UI workflows, and reserve **gpt-6-astra** ($10/$50 API rate, 250/1,250 credits/MTok) strictly for ambiguous architecture design or final adversarial adjudication, avoiding **Ultrafast** mode (8× subscription burn) and **Ultra** proactive subagent delegation on routine work8.  
**Instruction Discovery (AGENTS.md) and ChatGPT Projects:** Codex builds its instruction chain once per run by walking **top-down** from global (\~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md else \~/.codex/AGENTS.md) to the Git root and down to the current working directory, loading **at most one file per directory** (AGENTS.override.md \> AGENTS.md \> project\_doc\_fallback\_filenames) and concatenating them up to project\_doc\_max\_bytes (**32 KiB default**)15. Keep root AGENTS.md concise and place service-specific rules in subdirectory AGENTS.md files so they load only when \--cd targets that path57. In **ChatGPT Projects**, file uploads are capped at **40 files (Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu)**, **25 files (Plus/Go)**, and **5 files (Free)**58. Crucially, **Project Instructions completely override Global Custom Instructions** inside a project (global instructions do not load at all), and Google Drive links added as project sources **do not pre-sync** for automatic retrieval58. Configure sensitive client or trading projects to use **Project-only memory** so personal account memory cannot leak in or out58.  
**OS Sandbox, Auto-Review, and Prompt-Injection Defence:** Remove approval\_policy \= "untrusted" from all \~/.codex/config.toml files immediately; that setting is retired and prevents Codex or ChatGPT Work from starting23. Instead, mark untrusted repositories using \[projects."/path/to/repo"\] trust\_level \= "untrusted", which also prevents project-local .codex/ configs and hooks from auto-executing23. For local development, run sandbox\_mode \= "workspace-write" and approval\_policy \= "on-request" (enforced via macOS Seatbelt or Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap with network disabled by default)23. If you enable approvals\_reviewer \= "auto\_review", treat it as a reviewer swap (equipped with a 3-consecutive or 10-per-50 denial circuit breaker) rather than a deterministic security boundary60. Keep web\_search \= "cached" (the default in config.toml) so searches query OpenAI's pre-indexed cache rather than fetching live third-party pages, reducing exposure to live prompt injection, and never pass \--yolo, which disables the sandbox and flips web\_search to "live"59.  
**Staged Build Harness and Subagent Workflows:** For multi-phase engineering, adopt the official **Codex Staged Build Pattern** (developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/iterating-development-workflows-with-codex): strictly separate **"planning-only / harness-only"** turns (which write only GOALS.md, PLANS.md, and harness/build/phase-\<NN\>.md and are forbidden from touching application code) from authorised implementation turns, and record only decisions passing the **Materiality Test** in harness/context/phase-\<NN\>-\<slug\>-context.md48. Use /review for read-only diff audits (configurable via review\_model in config.toml), /side or /btw for ephemeral side questions, and /worktree for isolated branch execution62.

#### **7.3 Independent Playbook: Google Antigravity (App v2.23+, CLI agy v1.4.4+, SDK)**

**Architecture, Model Selection, and Quota Traps:** The Antigravity App (GUI), CLI (agy), IDE extensions (VS Code and Visual Studio 2026 in GA; JetBrains, Zed, Xcode, and Eclipse in Preview), and Python SDK (google-antigravity) run on a unified agent harness featuring native Git worktrees, visual diff/plan artifacts, and an integrated Chrome/PDF side panel18. Paid Google AI Pro (non-trial), Ultra, and Enterprise plans unlock first-party **Gemini 4 Argon** (gemini-4-argon, 1M context) and **Gemini 3.8 Flash** (gemini-3.8-flash), alongside third-party **Claude Sonnet 5.5** and **Claude Opus 5.5**18. **Sunset Alert:** Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, and GPT-OSS-120b will be removed from Antigravity on **2 November 2026**—migrate any pinned scripts or configs immediately18. Antigravity tracks two separate quota meters (5-hour and weekly) for (1) **Gemini models** and (2) **Claude/GPT models**18. However, official Gemini Enterprise documentation confirms that when you select third-party Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 in Antigravity, **lightweight background Gemini models continue running for client-side context management and summaries, consuming first-party Gemini tokens/quota alongside third-party Claude tokens**21. Keep "useG1Credits": false (AI Credit Overages \= Never) in \~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json unless you explicitly authorise pay-as-you-go overage spend21. Default to **Gemini 3.8 Flash** (medium or high thinking, $0.75/$3.75 introductory API rate) for fast repo iteration and subagents, and escalate to **Gemini 4 Argon** (high thinking, $2/$10 introductory rate through 30 November 2026, rising to $4/$20 on 1 December 2026\) for deep 1M-context reasoning and UI/browser verification18.  
**Rules (AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md / .agents/rules/\*.md) and Skills Migration:** Unlike Codex (which walks root-down and picks one file per directory), Antigravity walks **bottom-up** from the edited file's folder to the workspace root and **cumulatively combines all discovered rules** (AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, .agents/GEMINI.md, and .agents/rules/\*.md), with more specific directory rules taking priority on conflict66. Guard against three silent rule-discard hazards: (1) Antigravity performs **flat directory scanning** on .agents/rules/\*.md, silently ignoring nested subdirectories (such as .agents/rules/quant/pit.md) unless registered in .agents/rules.json66; (2) every file in .agents/rules/\*.md **must** start with valid YAML frontmatter declaring a snake\_case trigger (always\_on, model\_decision, glob, or manual), or Antigravity silently discards the file (camelCase alwaysOn or modelDecision fails)66; and (3) individual rule files are truncated at **24 KB** (after expanding @\[label\](path) includes), while all active always\_on and global rules share a **20,000-token aggregate budget** before the largest files are demoted to \- \<path\>: \<description\> pointers66. Additionally, because legacy .agents/workflows/\*.md files stopped working on **19 October 2026**, run /migrate-workflows in the Antigravity App to convert any remaining workflows to open-standard .agents/skills/\<name\>/SKILL.md bundles67.  
**Permissions, Sandboxing, Hooks, and Subagents:** Never select the Turbo preset (always-proceed / \--dangerously-skip-permissions), which disables sandboxing and grants unrestricted read/write access across the entire host filesystem (P1-08)1. Instead, configure **Default** or **Auto (Preview)** (toolPermission: "proceed-in-sandbox" and enableTerminalSandbox: true in \~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json), which confines shell execution inside macOS Seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap14. When authoring custom subagents in .agents/agents/\<name\>.md, verify every string in the tools: YAML array (view\_file, replace\_file\_content, grep\_search, run\_command), because **a single misspelled or unmapped tool name can cause the subagent process to hang indefinitely**70. Finally, use Antigravity's built-in /browser subagent—which drives a sandboxed Chrome instance with native Chrome DevTools MCP integration and records sessions as WebM videos—for automated UI/HTML verification and visual regression checks18.

## **PART III — DELIVERABLE C: STAGE 2 MULTI-PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE STUDY & INTEROPERABILITY VERIFICATION**

### **9\. Interoperability Reality Check and Instruction-Precedence Unification (P0-05, P1-07)**

Red-Team Finding P0-05 identifies a central flaw in naive multi-AI blueprints: **a shared Git repository does not synchronise active conversation histories, prompt caches, in-memory tool sessions, approval grants, or local auto-memories across Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity**1. Each harness persists its runtime state in a proprietary local directory outside the repository: Claude Code writes auto-memories to \~/.claude/projects/\<project\>/memory/22; OpenAI Codex writes local memories to \~/.codex/memories/ and SQLite session state to sqlite\_home (\~/.codex/sessions)57; and Google Antigravity writes session trajectories to \~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/\<conversationId\>/.system\_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl and sidecar data to \~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecar\_data/76.  
Furthermore, Red-Team Finding P1-07 warns that placing uncoordinated CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and GEMINI.md files in the same repository causes silent rule omissions and precedence conflicts across three incompatible discovery mechanisms1:

> 1. **The Claude Code CLAUDE.md vs. AGENTS.md Exclusivity Trap:** Official Claude Code memory documentation (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) states that if a repository has AGENTS.md and **no** CLAUDE.md, Claude Code reads AGENTS.md automatically; however, **if both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md exist, Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md only and ignores AGENTS.md unless CLAUDE.md explicitly imports it via @AGENTS.md**26.  
> 2. **The Opposite Directory-Walk Order Trap:** When operating inside a nested directory (such as src/quant/), **Codex** walks **top-down** (root AGENTS.md first, then src/quant/AGENTS.md second, so nested files appear later in the combined prompt and override earlier guidance) and stops loading files altogether once the combined byte count hits project\_doc\_max\_bytes (32 KiB default)15. Conversely, **Antigravity** walks **bottom-up** (src/quant/AGENTS.md first, then root AGENTS.md, plus all flat .agents/rules/\*.md files), truncates any single rule file exceeding **24 KB** (after expanding @\[label\](path) includes), and demotes the largest always\_on rule files to lightweight \- \<path\>: \<description\> pointers if the aggregate exceeds **20,000 tokens**66.  
> 3. **The Unified .agents/skills/ Convergence:** Both OpenAI Codex and Google Antigravity natively scan .agents/skills/\<name\>/SKILL.md using the Open Agent Skills Standard67, whereas Claude Code scans .claude/skills/\<name\>/SKILL.md22. Because POSIX symlinks are followed when scanning skill directories73, .agents/skills/ can serve as the single canonical skill library, symlinked to .claude/skills/.

#### **The Three-Tier Authoritative Policy & Adapter Architecture (Solving P1-07 and P0-05)**

To guarantee that all three runtimes load the exact same repository policies and skills without duplication, silent truncation, or state collisions, structure your repository across three clean architectural tiers15:

> 1. **Tier 1 — Authoritative Repository Policy & Skills Core:** Maintain a single canonical root **./AGENTS.md** (\<120 lines and \<6 KB, well below Codex's 32 KiB cap and Antigravity's 24 KB per-file cap) owning all shared build, test, lint, and architectural invariants alongside docs/ARCHITECTURE.md15. Store all reusable multi-step workflows once in **.agents/skills/\<name\>/SKILL.md** using standard YAML frontmatter (name and third-person description), and create a repository-relative symlink from **.claude/skills** to **../.agents/skills** so Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity discover the exact same skill bundles on demand53.  
> 2. **Tier 2 — Runtime-Specific Adapter & Sandbox Enclaves:**  
   * **Claude Code Enclave:** Place a thin 15-line **./CLAUDE.md** adapter at the repository root whose first line is **@AGENTS.md** (inlining the canonical policy up to 4 hops deep) followed only by Claude-specific \# Compact instructions, paired with path-scoped .claude/rules/\*.md (paths: YAML frontmatter) and deterministic PreToolUse/Stop hooks in .claude/settings.json24.  
   * **OpenAI Codex Enclave:** Reads ./AGENTS.md directly during its top-down walk, paired with .codex/config.toml (sandbox\_mode \= "workspace-write", approval\_policy \= "on-request", web\_search \= "cached") and SHA-hash-trusted .codex/hooks.json15.  
   * **Google Antigravity Enclave:** Reads ./AGENTS.md during its bottom-up walk alongside flat, snake\_case-validated .agents/rules/\*.md files (trigger: always\_on, model\_decision, or glob), paired with .agents/hooks.json, proceed-in-sandbox terminal isolation, and the /browser Chrome verification subagent14.  
> 3. **Tier 3 — Authoritative State & Deterministic Verification Gate:** Every agent writes code exclusively inside an isolated Git worktree (worktrees/agent-a/, worktrees/agent-b/), coordinates exclusively via schema-validated **tasks/\*.yaml** and **handoffs/\*.json** files on disk, and must pass the deterministic test and DuckDB PIT verification gate (pytest, dotnet test, mypy, pit\_as\_of) before any worktree branch is merged3.

### **10\. Evaluation of Competing Multi-Platform Architectures (Architectures A–F) & TCVSO Comparison (P1-06, P1-11)**

Per Sections 23–25 of MASTER\_RESEARCH\_PROMPT.md and Red-Team Findings P1-06 and P1-11, we evaluated the six candidate coordination architectures (Manual Coordination, Shared Repository, Central Orchestration, Event-Driven, Specialist Teams, and Hybrid) against single-agent and two-platform baselines across Workloads A, B, and C using our parametric TCVSO model1.  
![][image10]

#### **Architectural Verdicts and Dispositions (Architectures A–F)**

**Architecture A (Manual Coordination with Structured File Handoffs) — Disposition: Retain (Baseline for Solo Tasks & Workload C):** Under Architecture A, the human operator runs one primary platform and passes structured Markdown/YAML files (tasks/, handoffs/) to a second platform only when independent verification is required3. Its feasibility is **Currently Verified** across standard Pro, Plus, and Max subscriptions with zero webhook or API infrastructure overhead3.  
**Architecture B (Shared Git Repository with Worktree Isolation) — Disposition: Retain (Primary Recommended Multi-Platform Architecture for Workloads A & B):** Under Architecture B, Claude Code (claude \--worktree), OpenAI Codex (/worktree or codex exec), and Google Antigravity (Project Worktree mode) operate on isolated Git worktrees of the same local repository, governed by the unified ./AGENTS.md plus ./CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md) adapter and deterministic PreToolUse and Stop hooks15. Its feasibility is **Currently Verified**: worktree isolation prevents concurrent file-edit race conditions (T03) while enabling cross-family code review (codex exec \-m gpt-6.1-sol "/review") and browser E2E testing (/browser in Antigravity)11.  
**Architecture C (Centralised Custom Orchestrator Service) — Disposition: Reject for Solo/Small-Team Subscription Workflows; Conditional for API-Only SaaS Backends:** As highlighted by Red-Team Finding P0-05, consumer and seat-based subscriptions (Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Google AI Pro/Ultra) do **not** permit wrapping interactive CLI or consumer sessions inside an external automated multi-tenant orchestrator: Google Antigravity's FAQ explicitly prohibits wrapping consumer agy \-p headless runs inside third-party coding agents/applications21, and Anthropic restricts third-party harness consumption of subscription limits30. Building a compliant central orchestrator requires paying full API token rates across all three vendors (ANTHROPIC\_API\_KEY, OPENAI\_API\_KEY, GEMINI\_API\_KEY) plus maintaining custom state and retry infrastructure (£1.20+/run in our scenario model), yielding an estimated TCVSO of **£12.42** vs. **£5.76** for Shared Git Repository coordination on Workload A4.  
**Architecture D (Event-Driven Queues & Cron Sidecars) — Disposition: Conditional (Restricted to Read-Only Triage & Nightly Audits):** Event-driven automation is supported natively via Antigravity persistent **Sidecars** (sidecar.json with "builtin": "schedule" and agentapi new-conversation)76, Claude Code scheduled tasks (/schedule, /loop)26, and ChatGPT Work event-triggered automations (GitHub PR, Slack, or Gmail triggers)57. However, scheduled tasks in ChatGPT Work default to approval\_policy \= "never" where permitted by admin policy57, and idle /loop tasks in Claude Code silently drain 5-hour and weekly quotas while unattended5. Consequently, event-driven or scheduled runs should be permitted **only** in read-only or plan mode for nightly PIT data-integrity checks, dependency audits, or morning PR briefings, never for unattended write or deploy operations3.  
**Architecture E (Permanent Specialist-Agent Swarms / Agent Teams) — Disposition: Reject for Sequential or Write-Heavy Work; Conditional for Read-Only Parallel Exploration:** Official documentation for both **Claude Code Agent Teams** (code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams) and **Codex Subagents** (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents) explicitly warns against using multi-agent teams for sequential tasks, same-file edits, or write-heavy workflows due to approximately 7× token consumption in plan mode, merge conflicts, task-status lag, and broken /resume state for in-process teammates5. In our scenario model, a three-platform automated swarm on Workload B inflates TCVSO to **£14.90** vs. **£4.60** for a two-platform Git worktree handoff4. Use lightweight, bounded read-only subagents (Explore, explorer, research) instead8.  
**Architecture F (Pragmatic Hybrid: Shared Git Worktrees \+ Deterministic Oracles \+ Cross-Family Adversarial Review) — Disposition: Retain (Target Production Operating System):** Combines **Architecture B** (Shared Git Worktrees) with **Deterministic Software Oracles** (pytest, dotnet build, DuckDB bitemporal checks) and **Sequential Cross-Family Verification** (where Claude Code implements in a worktree, deterministic tests run via a Stop hook, and Codex gpt-6.1-sol or Antigravity /browser performs independent verification before human merge approval), achieving the lowest modeled TCVSO on complex tasks (£5.76 on Workload A and £4.60 on Workload B)3.

### **11\. Dynamic Task Allocation and Disagreement Adjudication Protocol (P1-12)**

To satisfy Requirements 25, 26, and 48 of MASTER\_RESEARCH\_PROMPT.md and Red-Team Finding P1-12 (Model agreement falsely treated as proof), **cross-model consensus is never accepted as verification**1. Because frontier models trained on overlapping web corpora frequently share correlated blind spots (tested in Adversarial Scenario T04), disputes between an implementing agent and a reviewing agent are adjudicated strictly by a four-tier **Evidence Hierarchy Oracle**1:

> 1. **Level 1 (Highest Authority — Deterministic Execution Oracle):** Automated test suite exit codes (pytest, dotnet test), static typecheckers (mypy, pyright, tsc), SQL/DuckDB bitemporal invariance queries, and cryptographic SHA-256 checksums1. If Agent A and Agent B agree that code is correct, but pytest exits non-zero, both models are overruled automatically3.  
> 2. **Level 2 (Primary Source & Ground-Truth Oracle):** Official vendor or exchange documentation fetched with an exact URL and verification timestamp, or raw immutable market filings in data/raw/1.  
> 3. **Level 3 (Adversarial Competing-Hypothesis Check):** When no deterministic oracle exists (such as architectural trade-offs or ambiguous research synthesis), the reviewing model (drawn from a **different vendor family** than the proposer—for example, OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol reviewing Anthropic claude-sonnet-5-5) must explicitly generate a **Rival Explanation / Falsification Hypothesis** before scoring the claim1.  
> 4. **Level 4 (Human Arbitration Gate):** Unresolved contradictions between Level 2 and Level 3 reviews halt the workflow and write a structured blocker entry into tasks/ACTIVE\_TASK.yaml for human decision3.

## **PART IV — DELIVERABLE D: STAGE 3 DATA ARCHITECTURE, BITEMPORAL INTEGRITY & SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION**

### **12\. Source-of-Truth Ownership Model (P1-09)**

Red-Team Finding P1-09 requires assigning a single authoritative owner for every data class so that Git files, database tables, vector indexes, platform memories, and report summaries never diverge silently1.

### **13\. Bitemporal Point-in-Time (PIT) Financial Data Architecture & Immutability Reconciliation (T05, P1-10)**

For Workload A (Python quantitative research, equity/FX screeners, and cTrader C\# cBot backtesting), look-ahead bias and survivorship bias are severe failure modes3. If a company restates its Q1 earnings on 10 August 2026, or if a data vendor backfills a delisted ticker's history without recording when the revision arrived, a standard database query run for a 1 June 2026 backtest cutoff will read the August restatement—leaking future information into the historical signal (T05)3. At the same time, Red-Team Finding P1-10 highlights that pure append-only immutability collides with legitimate vendor error corrections, license expirations, GDPR/privacy deletion requests, and local disk budgets1.  
![][image11]

#### **13.1 The Eight-Timestamp Bitemporal Schema (DuckDB \+ Parquet)**

Every financial, macroeconomic, or alternative-data observation ingested into data/pit\_store/ is stored in Zstandard-compressed Apache Parquet files queried via local **DuckDB** (requiring zero database server maintenance) using the following mandatory schema3:

SQL  
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pit\_observations (  
    observation\_id      UUID PRIMARY KEY,  
    entity\_id           VARCHAR NOT NULL,          \-- Permanent FIGI / internal perm\_id (never mutable ticker alone, preventing survivorship bias)  
    ticker\_at\_time      VARCHAR NOT NULL,          \-- Symbol active on event\_time (e.g., 'VOD.L')  
    metric\_name         VARCHAR NOT NULL,          \-- e.g., 'eps\_diluted', 'close\_unadj', 'split\_factor'  
    metric\_value        DOUBLE,                    \-- Nullable if redacted/tombstoned  
    currency            VARCHAR(8),  
    \-- Chronological & Bitemporal Timestamps (All stored in strict UTC TIMESTAMPTZ)  
    event\_time\_utc      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,      \-- Period end or bar close (e.g., 2026-03-31 23:59:59Z)  
    exchange\_tz         VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,      \-- IANA timezone (e.g., 'Europe/London') for DST-safe local reconstruction  
    published\_at\_utc    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,      \-- Official wire/exchange release timestamp  
    first\_avail\_utc     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,      \-- Vendor feed arrival timestamp  
    valid\_from\_utc      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,      \-- Start of business validity window  
    valid\_to\_utc        TIMESTAMPTZ,               \-- NULL if currently valid; set when superseded  
    ingested\_at\_utc     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,      \-- Immutable system transaction timestamp when written to pit\_store  
    superseded\_at\_utc   TIMESTAMPTZ,               \-- System transaction timestamp when a revision/correction arrived  
    revision\_num        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  
    \-- Provenance & P1-10 Immutability-Retention Reconciliation Fields  
    source\_vendor       VARCHAR NOT NULL,  
    raw\_payload\_sha256  CHAR(64) NOT NULL,         \-- SHA-256 of raw source payload  
    transform\_git\_sha   CHAR(40) NOT NULL,         \-- Git commit SHA of ingestion script  
    tombstone\_status    VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' \-- 'ACTIVE', 'CORRECTED', 'REDACTED\_PII', 'LICENSE\_EXPIRED'  
);

\-- Deterministic Point-in-Time (PIT) As-Of Query Macro:  
\-- Reconstructs the exact state known at any historical cutoff timestamp \`cutoff\_ts\`  
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO pit\_as\_of(cutoff\_ts) AS TABLE  
SELECT \* EXCLUDE (rn)  
FROM (  
    SELECT \*,  
           ROW\_NUMBER() OVER (  
               PARTITION BY entity\_id, metric\_name, event\_time\_utc  
               ORDER BY ingested\_at\_utc DESC, revision\_num DESC  
           ) AS rn  
    FROM pit\_observations  
    WHERE valid\_from\_utc \<= cutoff\_ts  
      AND ingested\_at\_utc \<= cutoff\_ts  
      AND tombstone\_status IN ('ACTIVE', 'CORRECTED')  
)  
WHERE rn \= 1;

This architecture resolves Finding P1-10 (Immutability vs. Correction/Deletion) through two mechanisms. First, for vendor errors and restatements, you never UPDATE or DELETE an existing financial observation; instead, you append a new row with revision\_num \= revision\_num \+ 1 and the current ingested\_at\_utc. Backtests executed with a cutoff\_ts prior to the correction automatically reconstruct the original data, while backtests with a cutoff\_ts after the correction see the corrected value3. Second, for privacy (GDPR) or licensing deletion requirements, sensitive payloads and licensed vendor blobs are stored in encrypted or partitioned payload files (data/payloads/vendor=\<v\>/), while pit\_observations retains only the cryptographic raw\_payload\_sha256 and sets tombstone\_status \= 'REDACTED\_PII' or 'LICENSE\_EXPIRED'1. Purging the payload partition satisfies legal erasure while preserving the immutable lineage log proving that a record existed and when it was lawfully purged1.

## **PART V — DELIVERABLE E & F: STAGE 4 SECURITY ARCHITECTURE, ADVERSARIAL RED-TEAM PROGRAMME & BENCHMARK SPECIFICATION**

### **15\. Upfront Security and Permission Architecture (P1-08, Requirements 38–39)**

To satisfy Red-Team Finding P1-08 (Security must be an upfront hard constraint, never an afterthought), a three-pillar security baseline must be configured **before** any agent is granted repository access1.

#### **15.1 OS Kernel Sandbox and Permission Enforcement**

In **Claude Code**, set the permission mode to manual or acceptEdits, disable bypassPermissions via "permissions": {"disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"} in .claude/settings.json, and configure explicit deny rules (which evaluate strictly in the order deny → ask → allow, overriding any specific allow rule)25:

JSON  
{  
  "permissions": {  
    "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable",  
    "deny": \[  
      "Read(.env\*)",  
      "Read(\~/secrets/\*\*)",  
      "Read(\~/.ssh/\*\*)",  
      "Read(\~/.aws/\*\*)",  
      "Edit(data/raw/\*\*)",  
      "Edit(.git/\*\*)",  
      "Edit(.claude/settings.json)",  
      "Bash(rm \-rf \*)",  
      "Bash(git push \*)",  
      "Bash(curl \*)",  
      "Bash(wget \*)"  
    \],  
    "allow": \[  
      "Bash(pytest \*)",  
      "Bash(mypy \*)",  
      "Bash(git status \*)",  
      "Bash(git diff \*)"  
    \]  
  }  
}

In **OpenAI Codex**, configure \~/.codex/config.toml with sandbox\_mode \= "workspace-write", approval\_policy \= "on-request", and web\_search \= "cached", and enforce \[permissions.filesystem\] deny\_read \= \["/\*\*/\*.env", "\~/.ssh", "\~/.aws"\] in requirements.toml23. In **Google Antigravity**, configure \~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json with "toolPermission": "proceed-in-sandbox", "enableTerminalSandbox": true, "allowNonWorkspaceAccess": false, and "useG1Credits": false, and never enable the Turbo preset1.

#### **15.2 Untrusted Content Isolation (T06) and Emergency Rollback**

All external web pages, PDFs, third-party GitHub issues, and MCP server outputs are classified as **untrusted data payloads** and never acquire instruction authority2. In Claude Desktop and claude.ai, never leave write-capable connectors (such as Gmail send, Drive trash/move, or GitHub write) enabled during automated **Research** runs, because Research mode invokes enabled connectors automatically without per-step approval prompts36. In Codex Cloud, configure external API credentials as **Network Secrets** restricted to explicit Allowed domains on port 443 rather than plain environment variables; the proxy substitutes the real credential in transit so the agent container only ever sees a placeholder value23.  
For emergency stops, press Esc or Ctrl+C in Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Antigravity CLI, or execute /stop in Codex CLI to terminate all background terminals spawned by the session18. Because all agent file writes occur inside dedicated Git worktrees (worktrees/\<task-id\>/) or checkpointed sessions, rollback is a single deterministic action: /rewind in Claude Code or Antigravity, or git worktree remove \--force worktrees/\<task-id\>18.

### **17\. Preregistered Controlled Benchmark Specification (Deliverable F — P0-03, Requirements 40–44)**

To eliminate Red-Team Finding P0-03 (AI self-scoring, cherry-picking, unequal tool access, and conflating unexecuted plans with measured results), all comparative benchmarks are governed by Requirement 44's strict separation of **Measured**, **Estimated**, and **Proposed** evidence1.  
**Measured Results (Executed & Verified in This Report):** Two foundational verification checks have been deterministically executed and verified for this report. First, **Prompt-Caching Payoff & 10-Turn Prefix Economics** were calculated directly from official 28 October 2026 rate tables across all 10 flagship models, confirming 78.5% to 85.2% 10-turn prefix savings and single-read break-even (0.26–0.28 reads) for 5-minute and 30-minute cache writes4. Second, **Bitemporal PIT Restatement Leak Prevention (T05)** was executed in Python/pandas on the VOD.L restatement dataset, proving that filtering on valid\_from \<= cutoff alone leaks the 2026-08-10 restatement (EPS \= 0.08) into a 2026-06-01 backtest, whereas the bitemporal predicate valid\_from \<= cutoff AND ingested\_at \<= cutoff reconstructs the exact historical truth (EPS \= 0.12)4.  
**Estimated Results (Explicit Parametric Scenario Models):** The **TCVSO Comparison Across Architectures A0–C1** (£4.60 to £15.37 across single-agent, two-platform, and three-platform setups) is an explicit parametric engineering model (4) incorporating official token rates, retry multipliers, and UK operator supervision valued at £1.00/minute.  
**Proposed Live Benchmark Suite (Preregistered — Blocked at Gate 2 Pending Your Gate 0 Sign-Off):** Once you approve the Gate 0 parameters in Section 3, live comparative trials will execute across a held-out 12-task benchmark manifest (BM-A1 through BM-C4):

> 1. **Workload A Tasks (4 tasks):** BM-A1 (DuckDB PIT as-of loader with corporate split adjustment), BM-A2 (cTrader C\# cBot async order-fill race condition bug fix), BM-A3 (Python pandas multi-factor equity screener vectorisation), and BM-A4 (Walk-forward backtest report generator with provenance manifest)3.  
> 2. **Workload B Tasks (4 tasks):** BM-B1 (Single-file regex/validation edit), BM-B2 (Multi-file FastAPI/React SaaS authentication refactor), BM-B3 (Interactive HTML team dashboard build plus headless Chrome UI verification), and BM-B4 (Interrupted-session recovery mid-refactor, T02)3.  
> 3. **Workload C Tasks (4 tasks):** BM-C1 (Primary-source API documentation verification), BM-C2 (150-page financial PDF structured table extraction against deterministic ground truth), BM-C3 (Adversarial false-consensus trap with misleading fixture, T04), and BM-C4 (Multi-session research synthesis with CLAIMS\_REGISTER.yaml audit)3.

To enforce experimental rigour (P0-03), **zero AI self-scoring is permitted**: every coding and data extraction task (BM-A1 to BM-B4, BM-C2) is scored exclusively by an independent, held-out deterministic test suite (pytest, dotnet test, or exact schema diff) located in a directory the agent is denied permission to edit (Edit(tests/oracle/\*\*) denied in settings.json)1. Every candidate configuration receives the exact same initial task specification (tasks/BM-\*.yaml), a maximum of **2 automated test-failure retries**, and a **15-minute wall-clock timeout**, with every failed turn, cache miss, permission prompt, and human intervention second logged in experiments/EXP\_LOG.jsonl across 3 counterbalanced repeats per task1.
